interactions.summary: A student rereads Dante's lines distinguishing animal and plant souls drawn from matter from human life breathed forth immediately by the chief good, then links that to resurrection through the creation of the first parents.

Jiang turns the Dante passage into a catechetical exchange about Adam: humans differ from animals because God breathes life into Adam directly, which Jiang glosses as God placing part of himself in humans as soul.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang question sequence with student answers

interactions.summary: After a student says the soul desires God, Jiang extends the point into a model of the universe in which everything humans do expresses a desire to return to God because a part longs to rejoin the whole.

claims.claim: The Dante passage says animal and plant souls are drawn from matter by holy rays and motion, but human life is breathed forth immediately by the chief good and therefore grounds the reasoning for resurrection.
Jiang says the proof that humans have a soul is the Dante line that human life is breathed forth immediately by the chief good.
Jiang anchors Dante's claim in Genesis by saying Adam is crafted from dust and then brought to life only when God breathes into him.
Jiang defines the soul as God putting a part of himself into humans.
A student answers that the soul's aspiration is to desire God, and Jiang sharpens this into the idea that humans fundamentally want to return to God because the part longs to rejoin the whole.
claims.temporal_scope: Student answer and Jiang elaboration stated on 2026-06-16.

claims.claim: Jiang says the desire to return to God is a fundamental logic of the universe and the hidden motive behind everything humans do, even when they do not know how to fulfill it.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang compresses Genesis into a blunt anthropological formula: God put a part of himself in us, and that part is what we call soul.
signature_moments.source_phrase: God put a part of himself in us
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is the packet's sharpest definition of soul and the hinge between human exceptionalism and desire for God.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang explains longing for God through the image of a severed finger wanting to be part of the whole body again.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The image gives memorable shape to his whole metaphysics of the soul as a separated part trying to return to origin.

signature_moments.moment: Everything humans do is recast as a veiled attempt to return to God.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Everything we do is because we want to return to God
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It turns the packet from a narrow Genesis gloss into a total model of motivation and cosmic desire.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang uses this phrase for the soul's drive to rejoin God, treating human desire as the movement of a separated part back toward its divine whole.

chronology_notes.note: This 2026-06-16 packet moves from the direct divine breathing that makes humans distinct to a full desire model in which soul means carrying part of God and therefore longing to return to him.
